articleTitle: Average Efficiency of Class-G Power Amplifiers
abstract: Class-G operation is an inexpensive and yet effective means of increasing the efficiency of audio power amplifiers (PAs) and amplitude modulators. A class-G PA consists of two or more parallel-connected class-B PAs with different supply voltages. Low-voltage segments of the signal are amplified by the low-voltage component of the amplifier, thus reducing power dissipation and increasing efficiency. The average efficiency of a class-G PA depends upon both the supply-voltage transition point and the amplitude distribution of the signal. Average efficiencies are computed for a number of signals that occur in AF amplification, full- carrier amplitude modulation, and envelope modulation of a linear RF PA. For typical peak-to-average ratios, an ideal, two-voltage class-G PA has average efficiencies in the range of 60 to 70 percent, in contrast to the 35 to 40 percent of an analogous class-B PA.

articleTitle: Adaptive Filter Techniques for Separation of Luminance and Chrominance in PAL TV Signals
abstract: Mass storage devices will be introduced in consumer TV products in the near future. After changing over TV signal processing from analog to digital, firstly the use of field and frame stores allows to do a big step towards a better picture quality, even in existing standards.

articleTitle: Digital Signal Processing Type Stereo FM Receiver
abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel method to demodulate both stereophnic FM and monophonic FM using Digital Signal Processig (DSP).

articleTitle: A System for Artifact Free NTSC Encoding and Decoding
abstract: This paper describes a method of NTSC compatible encoding and decoding of chrominance and luminance. Artifacts such as cross color, cross luminance, and "hanging dots" (an artifact usually appearing when conventional comb filters are used in TV receivers) are greatly reduced, while horizontal and vertical resolution is preserved. Special processing at the transmitter involving 8 to 10 line delays as well as during decoding at the receiver involving 10 to 12 line delays is required. With these modifications, NTSC can still be used in today's market place with increasing demands for picture quality.

articleTitle: A Solid State Color Video Camera with a Horizontal Readout MOS Imager
abstract: Since 1981 when we marketed world's first MOS color video camera1), we have been continuously improving the performance of this line of video cameras in order to match the market needs year by year2). We recognize, however, the performance we have achieved is not satisfactory enough.

articleTitle: Digital Signal Processing Technology For R-DAT
abstract: As one of consumer audio equipment, the CD (Compact Disc) player has come into wide use since its commercialization of 1982 for its high quality sound, easy operation and low price. The Direct Broadcasting Satellite (DBS) service has started in Japan in 1984. On the other hand, the Digital Audio Tape recorder (DAT) which has both recording and reproducing function and easy recording from these digitalized audio sources, is expected to be a next-generation audio product.

articleTitle: A High-Definition MUSE VCR with Analog Segment Recording Method
abstract: A high-definition VCR-MUSE VCR-has been developed along with the other high-definition TV components such as a MUSE-TV signal reception unit, a wide screen color display, and a video disc player.

articleTitle: On the Design of Segmented Arabic Numeric Display
abstract: In this paper, layouts for eight-, nine- and ten-segment Arabic numeric displays are introduced. As an exarnple, a BCD-to-ten segment-decoder, to be used for deriving the ten-segment-layout, is designed. An acceptable layout for a seven-segment-Arabic numeric display is also discussed.

articleTitle: New Automatic Focusing System for Video Cameras
abstract: Video cameras can be considered as a kind of substi tute for the human eye. They have a wide range of applications and as such, are in great demand. Advances in IC technology have improved video camera performance to the extent that it can rival that of the human eye. Yet, for even greater popularization of video cameras, improvement of performance and function is essential. The most important improvement in this area has been the development of a focusing system which is automatic. However, the considerable size of current automatic focusing systems has proved to be a major factor hindering the production of more compact models and, hence, their usability.

articleTitle: The DAT Conference. Its Activities and Results
abstract: Trials to improve the sound quality and functions of various types of audio equipment utilizing digital signal processing technology have been actively pursued recently. A method which records digital audio into a cassette type VTR was already standardized as a PCM Audio Processor and in use since 1979. In 1981 Compact Disc system was standardized and has been rapidly permeating through the market as a replacement for conventional disc records.

articleTitle: Servo Technology of R-DAT
abstract: The CTL tracking method is usually employed in VTRs etc.. in order to make the CTL tracking possible, the CTL signal synchronizing with reference signal is recorded on the tape and, during playback, the tracking servo works to maintain a constant phase between the drum revolution and the CTL signal. The CTL therefore, requires a stationary head to record or read the CTL signal, which opposes to simplify the mechanism. Furthermore, the manual tracking control is necessary, as the mechanical factors (for example, X-value, head mounting accuracy, and so on) introduce tracking error.

articleTitle: Lithium Copper Oxide Lithium Copper Oxyphosphate Battery Systems
abstract: Several lithiun anode primary cells are currently offered to electronic device designers. For safety considerations, only the so-called solid cathode systems are offered for consumer products. The ensuing presentation describes the features and performances of two solid cathode systems: Lithium Copper Oxide (Li-CuO) and Lithium Copper Oxyphosphate (Li-Cu4 O (PO4)2)

articleTitle: A Revised New Proposal For Standardization of Home Bus System for Home Automation
abstract: We first proposed in 1983 a plan for standardization of information distribution networks in a house called Home Bus System (HBS) to realize effective Home Automation (HA) in the world. In this paper we propose a revised new plan called HBS Version 1.2. This plan has been formulated after a number of experiments for various applications have been conducted for four years toward HA and two model houses are already in use for these experiments.

articleTitle: A Consumer USE Flicker Free Color Monitor Using Digital Signal Processing
abstract: With the spread of new video services such as teletext, captain and also DBS broadcasting, and with the pervasion of video package equipment like VCRs and optical video disc players, a TV receiver not only accepts on-air broadcasting programs but also is expected to work as a display monitor. A TV receiver as a monitor must necessarily be equipped with the improved picture quality within the current TV standards. Though the existing TV standard (NTSC) is highly sophisticated, its interlaced scanning, however, yields a poor result in terms of the vertical resolution. Especially, in case of a large size screen, the scanning line structure and the line flicker degrade the vertical resolution and sharpness significantly. In order to solve this problem, we have developed a practical intra-field adaptive line interpolating system with a small capacity of field memory and also designed a vertical contour compensation filter. In addition, by using the field memory in common, we have introduced a new function of "picture and still picture" with no cost increase.

articleTitle: Adaptive Equalizer for Teletext Receiver
abstract: We have developed a new fully-digital adaptive equalizer for teletext receivers which counteracts waveform distortion using teletext signals as reference signals and compensates equalized waveforms. This equalizer reduces the bit error rate vs. video signal S/N to 1/100 that without the equalizer.

articleTitle: Wide Band Video Signal Recorder Having Level and Linearity Corrector
abstract: Extensive works are now being carried out on the development of band compression techniques for the transmission of the high definition TV (HD-TV), which would be practiced in future by utiIizing one of the channels of 12 GHz band satellite broadcastings. In this, the bandwidth of HD-TV signal which occupies the bandwidth several times that of the present system, is compressed to less than 9 MHz. By making use of the above techniques. it is desired to provide a new video signal recorder with the capability of 9 M Hz band recordings.

articleTitle: 3-D Television, Movies and Computer Graphics Without Glasses
abstract: Television on standard bandwidth, theatre movies and sophisticated computer graphics-all in three dimensions without the need to wear special glasses are feasible with contemporary technology. This paper shows a viable approach to achieving the above with state of the art equipment. The 3-D results resemble a hologram extending to infinity with full color and without any special viewing zones or noticable anomallies over the entire viewing field.

articleTitle: Experiments on VTR Digital Signal Processing
abstract: In view of advantages that include multifunctional capability, improved performance and high reliability, digital signal processing technology has begun to be incorporated into television receivers. Application of digital technology to the servo circuits of consumer type video tape recorders (VTR) has already demonstrated cost reduction benefits.

articleTitle: Home Bus System (HBS) Interface LSI and ITS Standard Protocol Example
abstract: We first proposed in 1983 a plan for standardization of in-house information distribution networks called Home Bus System (HBS) to realize effective Home Automation (HA) in the world. In the HBS, digital data, audio and visual information of base-band and broad-band are transmitted on a single coax cable by frequency-division multiplex. In order to realize economical HA, a standard protocol for HBS was established and standardized interface LSIs were developed. These LSIs were incorporated into various equipment made by different manufacturers and usefulness of the HBS was verified by system experiments undertaken in two model houses. In this paper, the standard protocol and interface LSIs for the HBS base-band agreed on by many Japanese companies and a concrete control system for realization of HA are presented in detail.

articleTitle: Two Integrated Progressive Scan Converters
abstract: Before explaining the application and implementation of the two scan converters in detail, a brief description will be given of the digital environment in which these converters can be applied. Some general aspects of progressive scan and its impact on vertical bandwidth will also be discussed.

articleTitle: Magnetic Recording Characteristics of R-DAT
abstract: R-DAT requires a 76 kFRPI-linear recording density with an error rate of less than 10-2. Experimental results on carrier-to-noise ratio, equalization, error rate, overwriting, and durability, etc. are presented in this paper.

articleTitle: Home Informatization and Standardization of Home Bus
abstract: Advanced telecommunication systems and home-automation systems are being increasingly installed in Japanese homes.

articleTitle: The B-MAC Signal Format as Applied to 525 Line TV Systems and to H.D.T.V.
Proposed Interface Specifications for Home Bus
abstract: Today, more and more people are beginning to equip their homes with various information systems such as 1- line key-telephone systems or security alarm systems. A home bus, which manages signals and information, allows for their simple and neat installation.

articleTitle: TV VHF/Hyperband Tuner ICs
abstract: Two monolithic tuner circuits were developed to convert the desired TV-RF input channel of a VHF/ Hyperband to standard television IF for TV sets and set-top baseband converters. Not more than two switched bands are required for covering the complete frequency range of the 64 channels. Tracking is improved and local oscillator leakage is also reduced. The performance of CATV up/down converters is also improved if these ICs are used in the down-converter section.

articleTitle: One Chip 10 MHz RGB High Voltage Video Output Amplifier
abstract: Advances in high voltage integrated circuits allow the video amplifiers driving CRT cathodes to benefit from the advantages of integrated technology : extended performances, reliability, compactness and low power consumption.

articleTitle: Format of Pre Recorded R-DAT Tape and Results of High Speed Duplication
abstract: This paper presents the format of pre -recorded tape for playing back on a rotating-head digital-audio tape cassette recorder (DAT( ') and presents a technique for high-speed duplication of this tape. The sampling frequency of 44.lkHz is only used for pre-recorded tape and digital copying is not possible. The format also includes a wide track-pitch mode, which is used by producers of pre-recorded tape for high-speed contact duplication.

articleTitle: 16-BIT A/D Converter and D/A Converter for Digital Audio
abstract: The Compact Disc Player has made a rapid popularization of so called digital audio using a PCM technique. And this fall, Digital Audio Tape-recorder (DAT) is expected to be commercialized. The A/D and D/A converters are two of key devices for DAT, so it is required to realize high performance, low cost and low power consumption.

articleTitle: Digital Video Signal Processing in Home VTRs
abstract: Considerable attention has been given to digital signal processing technology to replace analog video signal processing circuits with digital circuits in home VTRs of VHS. Beta or other format[1]. Inherent capabilities of digital signal processing including (1) improvement in picture quality, (2) ease of providing multiple functions, (3) improvement in performances, and (4) considerable reduction both in component count of outboard analog devices and in the number of factory adjusted components, are becoming more and more realistic thanks to rapid advancement in semiconductor technology. On-chip digital signal processing is quite promising not only in reliability but also in economy in the long run.

articleTitle: Power Transistor Developments for Colour CRT Deflection
abstract: Todays colour CRT's have lower deflection energy requirements compared to the CRT's of, say, 12 years ago. The reason for this and the consequent reduction in deflection transistor peak current and peak voltage requirements, is the improved tube technology (narrow neck) and also improved deflection yoke design. A typical 22 inch 90 degree colour tv, today, requires the deflection transistor to operate at a peak collector current of less than 3A and a peak retrace voltage of 950V, whereas the older technology required the transistor, BU208, to operate at 4A and 1250V respectively.

articleTitle: Integrated Circuits for Tape Recorder Operated by Single Dry Battery
abstract: The latest portable tape recorders must be more compact, light-weight, and operate on a lower power supply, no more than a single 1.5V dry battery. Some of the latest integrated circuits for play-only tape recorders can operate on a single 1.5V dry battery, but integrated circuits for record-and-play cassette tape recorders still require two such batteries.

articleTitle: A Precision Mechanism for High Density Magnetic Recording of 8 MM VCR
abstract: Recent progress in the VCR technology is remarkable. This progress is much to owe the innovation of the high precision mechanism in the VCR equipment.

articleTitle: Single-Chip Multistandard Sound and Video IF Demodulator
abstract: This paper describes an integrated circuit designed to process both IF video and sound (AM & QBS) signals for many TV standards. It can therefore be used in multistandard television receivers, reducing the board area, component count and cost.

articleTitle: Digital Video in Consumer Applications
A Voice Activated Telephone
abstract: Telephones are already widely used in many areas, and various services come into wide use by means of public telephone networks today. The importance of a telephone set has been increasing as an access device to those services. Some telephone have additional functions, for example, automatic dialing, redialing, timer, etc.

articleTitle: Three Chip ICS Set Including Advanced Pre-Amplifier with Built-in Photo Detector for CD Players
abstract: In the CD system, the small disc size and subcode informations make the system very convenient, but the CD player requires more complex circuitry than analog record players. Several servo circuits are needed, such as focus servo, for example, that results in a more expensive product than conventional analog record players. The electronic circuit of the CD player is more expensive than that of the analog record player.

articleTitle: An Introduction to EIA IS-15 Standard Baseband (Audio/Video) Interface Between NTSC Television Receiving Devices and Peripheral Devices
Computer Controlled TV Hardware and Software Aspects
The THD Characteristics of the Phase detector
abstract: The paper presents an evaluation of the THD characteristics of the synmetrical and simple phase detectors, using exponential models of the detectors. By developing the output expressions into a series with Bessel-function coefficients, it is shown that, under certain conditions, the convergence is obtained. This approach results in relating the THD characteristics to other relevant electrical parameters of the circuits. Finally, a comparison is made between the simple and symmetrical detector with respect to their distortion characteristics.

articleTitle: Electrical Energy Monitoring and Control System for the Home
A Fully Integrated Filter Circuit for VCRs
abstract: In order to miniaturize VCRs, various components have been integrated with semiconductor circuits, but to date video filters such as luminance LPFs, emphasis filters, and chrominance BPFs have not been integrated. We have recently developed an integrated filter circuit for processing video signals. The new circuit was fabricated using a new bipolar process called the Hiplanar process and has been applied to a dynamic emphasis IC for VCRs. Because this filter circuit operates up to 10 MHz, any video filter can be integrated by the same means.

articleTitle: Progress Report: RF Cable Interface and Decoder Interface Working Groups
abstract: Standards committee progress is often painfully slow. To a newcomer, especially someone accustomed to the "fast lane," this activity can be quite frustrating. There are several points to be made about this. Firstly, if cable interface and decoder interface standards were easy to achieve, they'd have been agreed to a long time ago. There's been pressure for an extended period of time. Secondly, the issues being settled are delicate points involving trade-offs which Impact the economics and performance of two industries. These two industries have a history short on cooperation and long on confrontation. Fortunately, the trend toward cooperation is on the up swing.

articleTitle: Magnetic Tape and Cartridge of R-DAT
abstract: The specifications of R-DAT cartridges and tapes have been set by common consent in a DAT conference held in Japan. A study committee has been studying, the details of the specifications. A cartridge size of 73x54xlO.5mm has been decided based on the results of a questionaire conducted on all members of the DAT Conference. The cartridge has a dust-free structure with its inside equipped with a brake to prevent the hub from rotating freely and its outside, the lid and slider. Magnetic-metal-powder coated tapes are used for recording, and a recording tape 13um (nominal) tick will provide a recording time of two hours.

articleTitle: A Monolithically Integrated 128 Led-Driver and Its Application
abstract: Electrophotographic printing is one of the most attractive non-impact printing methods because it can be fast, compact, and of high quality. All electrophotographic technics need a light source of some kind, for instance a laser source or an LED array. The loser illuminates one point at a time and, therefore, requires a scanner to print a line serially. In contrast a linear LED array prints a whole line at a time. Due to the combination of active emission and parallel printing capability an LED-bosed printing unit can be made very compact and power efficient.

articleTitle: D2-MAC-A New Feature for Digital TV
Configuration and Performance of a Home Bus using Slotted Flag Control
abstract: In this information age, making available information in the home is desirable for user need diversification. To promote this, it is necessary to integrate telephone, home security and telecontrol equipment using a home bus.

articleTitle: Development of HDTV Receiving Equipment Based on Band Compression Technique (MUSE)
abstract: It is about sixteen years since the Investigation of High-definition television (HDTV) system was started by NHK (Japan Broadcasting Corporation), and its outstanding picture quality has already demonstrated on various occasions.(1)

articleTitle: Intelligent Non-Volatile Memory for Smart Cards
abstract: Plastic cards with an imbedded semiconductor chip, which is of the same size as the most frequently used credit or check cards, are in the process of radically changing the world of finance and security system.

articleTitle: Advanced Digital Television System
abstract: This paper will give an architectural overview of an advanced digital televisicn system which utilizes the latest VISI technology, fast digital signal proessing ard frame buffer. This digital design aproach will lead to a cost-effective chip set that will produce improved quality, and higher definition TV picture for either the NTSC or PAL system.

articleTitle: AN Electronic Still Camera System
abstract: Recently, great interest has been shown in electronic still camera systems which record still picture informations on a small magnetic disc called "Still Video Floppy". The 2 inch size video floppy has 50 main tracks to store signals and one special track(Cue Track) to control the main tracks. The signal on one track corresponds to one field picture, therefore two adjacent tracks are used to record a frame picture.

articleTitle: A CMOS Dual Port Memory with Serial Read/Write Function for Graphic Systems
abstract: As the cost per bit of semiconductor memories and the price of small computer systems continue lowering, personal work stations or computer aided design (CAD) systems come to be used widely. The market for graphic display systems also expands, because interactive operations between users and such systems are unavoidable in personal usage.

articleTitle: CCD Delay Line For Video TBC
abstract: Up to now, TBC (Time Base Corrector) of optical video disc player has been made of mirror and coil. This mechanical TBC has disadvantages of high power dissipation, and delicateness against shock or vibration. Since a reliable TBC has been demanded, we have developed an electronic variable delay line using CCD in order to replace the mechanical TBC.

articleTitle: A Multistandard Chip Set for VHS VTR's
abstract: Based on the four chip set for signalprocessing-presented at the ICCE in 1984-we decided to develop a two chip set with higher scale integration. Additional stages for feature modes in all speeds and the capability for "HIGH Q" and NTSC/PAL/SECAM multistandard are also included. The range of new 5 volt low power devices will be completed by a CCD-Delayline, a SECAM Ident IC for SECAM ME processing, a SECAM L processor, a picture improvement IC and two supporting add on IC's. This chip set gives the setmaker the flexibility to design a full range of VTR's-from "economy" versions up to "top class" models-including one or more standards, with very attractive and competitive prices.

articleTitle: AN Edge Enhancement Algorithm Using a Polynomial Transformation
abstract: The paper describes a new algorithm proposed for improving the subjective quality of picture by means of contour enhancement. The method applies on digitalized pictures. The algorithm is based on a transient detection scheme followed by a polunomial transformation. The possibility of choosing a specific polynomial makes this new method useful for various applications, such as chrominance contour improvement on television pictures or edge enhancement for picture coding.

articleTitle: Digital TV
abstract: Digital TV, from a TV manufacturer's standpoint, could simply imply replacement of the conventional analog video signal processing system in a color TV receiver by digital signal processing. This concept could also be extended to the low level audio and deflection systems portion of the TV set. Digital TV could also imply the addition of "digital" features such as Picture-in- Picture (PIP), Multi Picture-in-Picture (MPIP), Freeze Frame, Zoom, etc. and picture performance improvements such as Progressive Scan, motion-compensated Noise Reduction and Frame Combing, etc. These latter schemes need storage of a field and/or frame of video information. This paper gives an overview of the above concepts and addresses them from several viewpoints, including implementation, cost, manufacturing advantages, picture quality etc.

articleTitle: A Digital Signal Processing Approach to Multichannel Television Sound Decoding
abstract: The introduction of the Multichannel TV sound standard by television broadcasters offers a new opportunity for digital audio. The system described in this paper offers a complete implementation of the BTSC MTS standard using digital signal processing techniques.

articleTitle: A Very High-Speed Digital Signal Storing Device
abstract: A scheme of storing very high-speed digital signals is presented, which requires no special components other than conventional IC's and only one clock period for recording data. By using commercially available ECL for example, the rate of data recording can reach as high as 150 MHz. This method is suitable for both single and multiple channel data recordings.

articleTitle: Resonant Degaussing for TV and High Definition Color Monitors
abstract: In a shadow mask color picture tube, accurate landing of the red, green and blue beams on the corresponding phosphors on the screen is obtained by careful design of the electron optics and the magnetic deflection system. However, the earth's magnetic field can deflect the beams from the intended color to adjacent phosphors of different color, causing purity errors on the screen.

articleTitle: Development of High-Definition Video Copy Equipment
abstract: High-definition video copy equipment with picture quality almost simulating photo prints has been developed. A sublimation dye thermal transfer method is used to give prints which are A5 in size and have a printing resolution of 8 dots/mm.

articleTitle: Very Low Voltage Operation IC's for Portable Radio Receiver Use
abstract: Recently, by the benefit of integrated circuit and micro mechanism very small and light weight portable equipments are introduced to the consumer market. These equipments require the IC operating at very low voltage and low power consumption because of the limited dry cell number and weight. The final target for this purpose is to realize ICs operating by single cell.

articleTitle: A Zoom Lens System with New Infrared Autofocus Mechanism
abstract: In order to realize a compact and high-performance video camera, solid-state-imager,(1) auto-white-balance and auto-focus-mechanism (2) have been developed. As a result of these efforts, almost consumer video camera have come to install these functions.

articleTitle: Decoder Restored SYNC-THE Key to EIA Baseband Interface Standard IS-15
abstract: Decoder Restored Sync (DRS) provides feedback allowing decoder control of receiver AGC. The need for, and format of DRS are explained. The closed-loop performance of a television receiver/baseband cable descrambler system is examined under worst case conditions for single and differential decoder references.

articleTitle: Driving Current Dependence of Aging Drift in 600MHz Band Saw Resonators
abstract: SAW resonators driven at high driving levels are known to suffer from degradation of electrical arac- characteristics caused by stress induced metal-migration in the aluminum thin film transducers and reflectors(1), (2). The migration phenomenon is similar to an electro-migration which has been observed in aluminum film conductors of semiconductor integrated circuit.

articleTitle: Head Actuator Servo for VTR Using Four Frequency Pilot Signals
abstract: A recent tendency is to employ narrower recording tracks essential for the high density video recordings. However, due to the track linearity variation caused by mechanical accuracy limitation, assurances for the tape interchangeabilties are increasing difficulties. As in Fig. l(a), unless the recording and its reproduction are performed on the same recorder, the loss of reproduced output due to the miss-tracking is unavoidable. As shown in Fig. l(b), the tracking error signal generated in this case, generally contains relatively higher frequency component above 60Hz, and since the tape transport servo mechanism is not extended to cover this higher frequencies, the heads can not trace the non-linear recorded tracks.

articleTitle: Decoder IC for an Automatic Video Program Identification System (VPS)
abstract: A special coded identification signal transmitted on line 16 of the vertical interval along with the program enables an automatic video program identification. Receiving equipment (i.e. VCR) with VPS circuitry can be activated automatically when the proper VPS code is found. A VPS decoder IC for applications in VCR and TV receivers is decribed.

articleTitle: Advanced Television Systems
abstract: The United States Advanced Television Systems Committee (ATSC) was formed in 1983 to coordinate the development of national technical standards for advanced television systems and to develop proposed national positions for presentation to the Department of State for purposes of developing United States positions with international organizations.

articleTitle: A New Magnetic FLUX Control SMPS and the Multiscan Deflection System
abstract: There is now a considerable demand for monitors capable of displaying very fine-grained characters and graphic images. These monitors are needed for use with 16-bit high-resolution personal computers with an increased horizontal scanning frequency for producing higher vertical resolution and for displaying RGB source signals such as high-resolution VIDEOTEX. Multiscan monitors which can detect the horizontal sync signal and automatically adjust the display by themselves are being increasingly marketed. Most of these monitors incorporate an insulated-type Switched Mode Power Supply (SMPS).

articleTitle: Integrated Circuit Decoder for the German Two-Channel TV Sound System using Switched Capacitor Techniques
abstract: Switched-capacitor techniques offer, in the right environment, the possibility to integrate entire processing sub-systems with practically no requirement for external components. An example of one such environment is the audio processing and condition identification environment in the German TV stereo sound system. Presented here is an I.C. which performs a complete sound processing and transmission status identification on one-chip. Stereoton* is produced in 5 micron silicon-gate CMOS. It operates at 12 volts D.C. and consumes 35 mA. M.P.U. control is through a 2-line bus.

articleTitle: A New Tuning System for use in AM Stereo Receivers
Wideband Distribution Problems in Cable
abstract: This paper covers alternatives in today's broadband CATV Distribution. An overview of important system parameters affecting cable performance will be given. A number of amplification and transmission methods as well as environmental effects will be discussed. Finally, failure modes and other system problems will be addressed.

articleTitle: Design of Generalized n-way Power Divider for CATV and/or MATV Systems
abstract: The new design theory of a generalized n-way power divider with arbitrary dividing ratios, for CATV and/or MATV systems, which consists of ideal multi-winding transformers and resistors only was presented. Since the circuit elements have not frequency dependance, the proposed power divider is to be of extremely broad band-width.

articleTitle: High Performance FM-IF IC for Systems with Search Tuning Stop and Multipath Interference Detection
abstract: Mobile antennas, located close to the ground, e.g. receivers in vehicles, are subject to continuously changing field strength levels. Through the effects of scattering and reflection, partial waves are superimposed on the direct signal depending on time and location and lead to interferences due to multipath (MP) reception.

articleTitle: A New Car Radio with Recording and Playback Functions
abstract: The paper describes a high performance car radio and the recording and playback features in the radio. These features allow the driver who has failed to hear some important information to listen to the missed words again. It is based on speech compression and reproduction techniques. In this paper some speech compression techniques are discussed.

articleTitle: Tuning of Nonstandard TV Picture Carriers
abstract: In numerous households with video services the input signal to the tuner of a TV receiver may not necessarily be provided by an antenna, but may be a CATV signal or originate in a home instrument like a VCR or a video game. The RF carrier frequencies of signals not received directly from commercial TV stations do not necessarily conform with the FCC standards. For example, the picture carrier frequency of a channel may be offset by several megahertz from the FCC specified value. The purpose of this paper is to describe a reliable method of automatically tuning nonstandard TV signals with offsets as large as 3 MHz.

articleTitle: A low cost high performance picture display for photovideotex
Channel 6/Educational FM Interference in TV Receivers
abstract: Channel 6 and FM station signals across the country have been battling for years for supremacy in the picture of a television receiver. Since April 1976, with the publication of Notice of Proposed Rule Making, Docket 20735, the FCC has been attempting to define the protection ratio between FM and Ch. 6; and to deal with the ever increasing backlog of applications for noncomnercial, educational FM broadcast stations which would occupy the 88-92 MHz band, the major area for sources of interference to TV receivers.

articleTitle: Image and Oscillator Interference on Cable Television Systems
abstract: If the television set manufacturer chooses as a tuning mechanism a double conversion type of tuner where the IF frequency is above the highest frequency on the cable system and the local oscillator for the first mixer is a fundamental oscillator (not a doubler) whose frequency is always above this IF frequency, then there is no image or oscillator leakage problem. This is the typical system used in cable converters.

articleTitle: Fully Automatic Self Alignment of TV-Tuners
HF2C, A New Analog/Digital Bipolar Technology for Videoprocessing IC'S
abstract: HF2C is a bipolar technology which combines analog devices and IIL gates. This technology is well suited to linear applications which require digital capability, high packing density, high speed and low current operation. Process technology, device characteristics and the design of a high performance video processor are presented.

articleTitle: Compatibility of NTSC Color Decoders with HDTV Signals
abstract: The japanese proposal in respect to a standard for a High Definition Television sjstem (HDTV) presents, due to its greater development degree, the highest probability of universal adoption.

articleTitle: THE IC Card and Consumer Electronics - The American Market
abstract: Having spent most of my professional career in the technology of plastic cards, my background in consumer electronics is limited. I can see, however., many places that the smart IC card can fit the industry. In this paper I shall discuss the most important and imminent uses of the card. certainly other places will occur to you as these lectures acquaint you with the structure and abilities of the IC card.

articleTitle: High Power Consumer Replaceable Lithium Manganese Dioxide Batteries
abstract: In the late 1970's two lithium systems became available to consumers. These were lithium manganese dioxide (Li/MnO2) and lithium carbon monofluoride (Li/CFx)n. Both are 3 bolt systems. They are presently the predominant lithium systems available in the consumer marketplace. The former system is reviewed here.

articleTitle: Processing of IF Television Signals in a Multistandard Environment
abstract: The reception technology of domestic receivers for the earth distributed T. V. signals has stabilized itself in a more or less standard pattern: a channel selector, provided with a mild selectivity, picks up a specific R.F. T.V. channel and converts it into an Intermediate Frequency signal. This signal is subsequently submitted to a main frequency selecting device, the I.F. selectivity, followed by an I.F. processor, whose output delivers the baseband composite video signal.

articleTitle: A Color Flat CRT and its Application
abstract: Since V.K.Zworykin made practical use of the cathode ray tube possible in 1929, its high luminous efficiency, uniformity, wide range of brightness, wide angle of visibility and ease of production rapidly rendered it the principal display medium for television.

articleTitle: A Digitally Controlled Tone & Volume Circuit for Autosound Systems
abstract: A microprocessor controlled tone and volume circuit for automotive applications has been integrated in a CMOS technology. Very few external components are required while a high level of performance is achieved. Stereo source selection, volume, tone, loudness, balance and fader functions are provided.

articleTitle: Low Noise Integrated SHF Converter for Satellite TV Broadcasting
abstract: We have successfully developed a high performance SHF converter for satellite TV broadcasting system, which converts the 12GHz incoming signal down to the 1GHz signal.

articleTitle: A Digital Controlled Videoprocessor IC for Color TV - Set
abstract: A digital-controlled analog signal processing circuit achieves both contrast and saturation functions of this bus-controlled videoprocessor.

articleTitle: Hardware and Software Aspects of Computer-Controlled TV
Digital Signal Processing for Memory Features in TV Applications
Housekeeping Application with Bus Line and Telecommunication
abstract: The functions of this system are Home Security, Energy Control, Tele-Control, Tele- Monitor and Auto-Dial and this system has a Bus Line between a Main-Controler and Sub-Controllers. For standardization of this Application system, the main procedure are described.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Coax and Twisted Pair Home Bus
abstract: Some problems that should be solved before establishing a home bus system and the home bus system that has already solved problems are described below.

articleTitle: A CD-ROM Data Retreiver IC
abstract: The functional structure of a programmable CD-ROM data retreiver IC is discussed here. The chip operates on serial streams of CD data from an already available EFM demodulator/decoder chip, designated here as CD2A, and performs a number of data manipulations such as; descrambling, reformatting and CRC error checks, etc. The chip can be programmed to locate and transfer desired data blocks and/or bytes to a host processor through an I/O bus interface. Slow serial data transfers, e.g. RS232, can also be performed, if needed by utilising the appropriate facilities of the system's microcontroller.

articleTitle: Interference Problems in Proposed Spectrum Sharing Between FM Land Mobile Radio and UHF Television
abstract: On June 20, 1985 under general Docket No. 85-172 the FCC issued a Notice of Proposed Rule Making entitled "Further Sharing of the UHF Television Band by Private Land Mobile Radio Services."

articleTitle: Minitel and Smart Card: A Total Synergy
abstract: In the last ten years, we have run in France a number of tests on the leading edge of new technologies. Among those, spreading very quickly from the beginning on, Videotex is now a true, real habit of the consumer's life.

articleTitle: Resolution Enhancement in a 3 Chip RGB Camera Using Offset Technique
abstract: Already a few years after the fundamental development of solid state imagers these devices represent a serious competition to conventional pick up tubes. While the use of imagers in colour TV cameras is possible with some restrictions in the resulting picture quality today, the solid state sensors cannot meet the requirements of the present studio technique by simple substitution of tubes by imagers.

articleTitle: 8 Bit Convertors for Video Applications
abstract: Increasingly, the improvement of the quality of TV pictures and new features as satellite TV and scrambled TV lead to digital processing of the video signal. As a consequence, A/D and D/A converters able to handle video signals become essential in this approach. Of course such devices are now commercially available and are used in a variety of professional pieces of equipment, but their price is hardly compatible with their use in a consumer TV set. In such applications the integration of a number of components allows the reduction of the price of the overall system to a level commercially acceptable. This was the background of a study* of A/D and D/A converters carried out at LEP** with the objective of reducing drastically the component count around each converter.

articleTitle: Monolithic Fiber Optic Video Signal Transmission Module
abstract: Fiber optic transmission systems have been applied over a variety of areas, but fiber optic video signal transmission systems are not so spread as fiber optic data transmission systems.

articleTitle: A Microcomputer Chip With Non-Volatile Shadow Ram for Consumer Applications
abstract: Using a double cell approach combining static and non-volatile memory, a dedicated microcomputer chip includes a memory which operates at the full micro speed, yet can retain data even when the power supply has been removed. Applications of the device include electronicect- onic tuning systems, analog value settings, white goods, smart telephones, electronic odometers and other applications tions requiring non-volatile data storage.

articleTitle: The Residential Power Circuit as a Communication Medium
abstract: This paper is a summary of work done to characterize the residential power circuit as a communication medium. Here the term residential power circuit refers to that part of the power circuit on the secondary side of the distribution transformer. This circuit is often used for communication signals for controlling appliances, security devices, and for other purposes. The frequencies of most interest in these systems range from about 100 to 200 kHz. The interface to this circuit is usually a 120 V or 240 V receptacle used to deliver power. These communication systems are called residential power line carrier systems. Other types of power line carrier are distribution line carrier and transmission line carrier both of which are used by the power utilities for communications purposes.

articleTitle: An Experimental Digital Video Recording System
abstract: The feasibility of digital video recording for consumer applications has been investigated with a view to a high image quality with full PAL bandwidth. A dominant boundary condition was that there should be no loss of maximum playing-time as compared to the analog system. To meet this requirement, compression of the digitized video signal with DPCM and Hadamard Transform coding has been applied. Other requirements were the use of standard V2000 mechanics, ferrite heads and chromium-dioxide tape.

articleTitle: Teletext for the World
abstract: So far, World System Teletext has been used mainly for European languages. This paper discusses how it can be exploited to handle some of the writing systems used in other parts of the world. Possible coding methods are suggested and the design of suitable decoders is considered. By way of illustration of the techniques involved, the writing systems of Arabia, India, Korea and Japan are taken as examples.

articleTitle: Super Compact Plastic Projection Lensen for Projection Televisions
abstract: A new compact plastic lens is proposed to meet demands for further reduction of a projection TV cabinet size while maintaining high image quality with a newly developed stop for cutting off undesirable sagittal aberration.

articleTitle: Digital Audio Data Transmission in a Coaxial Cable Environment
abstract: Cable operators are currently presented with multiple vendor options when considering the addition of high quality audio services. Initial product selection by the operator will serve to communicate the minimum acceptable functional and performance requirements to manufacturers. System operators are therefore uniquely positioned to demand the best in quality, performance and economy from future audio products. Technical product field testing provides the operator with preliminary information which may be valuable in determining how to invest capital for a new service.

articleTitle: Single Chip Multisystem AM Stereo Decoder IC
abstract: We developed a single chip AM stereo decoder IC, which can demodulate three AM stereo systems, and automatically switch to the receiving system.

articleTitle: 1986 Index IEEE Transactions on Consumer Electronics Vol. CE-32
abstract: This index covers all technical items - papers, correspondence, reviews, etc. - that appeared in this periodical during the year, and items from previous years that were commented upon or corrected in this year. Departments and other items may also be covered if they have been judged to have archival value. The Author Index contains the primary entry for each item, listed under the first author's name. The primary entry includes the coauthors' names, the title of the paper or other item, and its location, specified by the publication abbreviation, year, month, and inclusive pagination. The Subject Index contains entries describing the item under all appropriate subject headings, plus the first author's name, the publication abbreviation, month, and year, and inclusive pages. Note that the item title is found only under the primary entry in the Author Index.
